campoCriptana.title: Campo de Criptana
campoCriptana.excerpt: Just a few kilometers from Arenales de San Gregorio, Campo de Criptana offers an experience that goes beyond its famous windmills.
campoCriptana.content:
## Introduction

Just a few kilometers from our accommodation in Arenales de San Gregorio lies Campo de Criptana, one of those places that, even if you've seen it in photos, surprises you when you're there. Its windmills dominating the plain are part of La Mancha's history and the image we all have of Don Quixote. But beyond the postcard, what really captivates you is the feeling of the place.

Climbing up to the windmills and seeing how the landscape stretches out around you is something that transmits tranquility. It's not just a tourist spot, it's an open, silent space where everything seems to slow down.

## Sunset, the best moment

If there's a special time to visit Campo de Criptana, it's at dusk.
When the sun begins to set, the sky fills with warm colors: oranges, pinks, violets... and the windmills are silhouetted against the horizon creating an unforgettable image. It's one of those sunsets that invite you to stand still, to watch and let time pass.

You can be chatting with someone, taking photos or just sitting, but in the end we all end up the same: watching in silence.

## Walk, history and calm

Walking through the Albaicín neighborhood with its white houses is very pleasant.

If you like photography, you'll find yourself looking for angles over and over again.

And if you simply need to disconnect, here it's easy to take a deep breath and relax your mind.

## Very close to our accommodation

One of the advantages of staying in Arenales de San Gregorio is precisely that tranquility and proximity to places with so much magic like this one. You can go in the afternoon, watch the sunset and return without rushing, enjoying the journey.

Campo de Criptana is not just visited, it's felt.
And if you come, you'll understand perfectly why its sunsets stay stored inside.

casaMedrano.title: Casa Medrano
casaMedrano.excerpt: This historic corner combines culture and serenity in a simple but meaningful space. A brief, intimate visit perfect for enjoying a quiet afternoon with a touch of history.
casaMedrano.content:
## Introduction

Just a few minutes by car from our accommodation in Arenales de San Gregorio lies Argamasilla de Alba, a town that holds one of the most curious and special places in La Mancha: Casa Medrano, known as the supposed prison of Cervantes and the place where Don Quixote de la Mancha may have begun to be written.

This building, simple on the outside, hides a story that captures attention as soon as you learn about it. It is said that Miguel de Cervantes was imprisoned here in the 16th century, and that during that time he may have begun to shape the work that, over the years, would become one of the most important novels in world literature.
Being there, in the same room where it's believed he wrote part of Don Quixote, has something special. It's one of those places where history feels close, almost real.

## A place that mixes culture and tranquility

Casa Medrano is not a large or overwhelming museum. And precisely because of that, it's pleasant.
You don't need to be a deep literature lover to enjoy it. It's a light, interesting plan, perfect for a quiet morning or afternoon.

Close to home and easy to visit

It's a short, comfortable outing with that historical touch that makes the trip more special.

lagunasRuidera.title: Lagunas de Ruidera
lagunasRuidera.excerpt: Its waters linked by waterfalls and cascades create a unique landscape, ideal for walking, relaxing or enjoying activities like kayaking, paddle surfing, cycling or hiking trails.
lagunasRuidera.content:
## Introduction

Discover the Lagunas de Ruidera: a natural paradise near our accommodation in Arenales de San Gregorio
If there's one place we always recommend to those staying at our house in Arenales de San Gregorio, it's undoubtedly the Lagunas de Ruidera. Just a few kilometers away lies one of the most beautiful and surprising natural spaces in Castilla La Mancha, perfect for disconnecting and enjoying nature in its purest form.

The most special thing about this place is how the water links between lagoons through small waterfalls and natural cascades, creating a landscape that, honestly, you don't expect to find here. You don't need to be a hiking enthusiast to enjoy it; simply walking, sitting by the water or doing an easy trail already reconnects you with everything.

## A place to do whatever you feel like: relaxation or adventure

The Lagunas de Ruidera are very versatile. You can go to spend the day in a relaxed way, bring something to eat, a fresh drink and find some shade by the water.
But, if you're more into moving around, you have many options:
- Hiking trails and viewpoints with impressive views
- Kayak and paddle surf to enjoy the water in a different way
- Swimming areas in summer, ideal for cooling off
- Cycling on accessible and well-marked paths

And if you go with children, it's a perfect plan: clear water, safe areas, nature and space to play without rushing.

## The comfort of staying in Arenales de San Gregorio

One of the advantages of our accommodation is precisely the tranquility of the surroundings. Arenales is a small, cozy town where you can be at peace. And the best thing is that from here you can go to the Lagunas de Ruidera in a short time, without having to stay in more crowded or touristy areas.

If you're looking for nature, clean air and a beautiful place to spend a few days, the Lagunas de Ruidera are a sure hit. And from our accommodation you'll have the perfect combination: getaway, rest and adventure, all at your own pace

cooperativaVinas.title: Virgen de las Viñas: Art, Tradition and Wine
cooperativaVinas.excerpt: Art, Tradition and Wine represents the philosophy of Virgen de las Viñas, the reflection of the experience that transfers its essence to the wines we produce.
cooperativaVinas.content:
## Art, Tradition and Wine

Art, Tradition and Wine represents the philosophy of Virgen de las Viñas, the reflection of the experience that transfers its essence to the wines we produce.

Enjoy the three spaces that combine our philosophy.

## The Wine Press - Ethnological Museum

Tradition is present in the Wine Press, the heart of the winery that has not stopped beating since its origins. An emblematic building that currently houses the Ethnological Museum. A collection of tools and utensils that help remember how the first settlers of Tomelloso worked in the vineyards.

## The Centenary Caves

Discover our caves carved in a limestone slab, recently restored and open to the public to learn firsthand how they were used 100 years ago to produce and store wine.

## Infanta Elena Contemporary Art Museum

The visit to the "Infanta Elena" Contemporary Art Museum will give you the opportunity to experience firsthand the art that breathes inside Virgen de las Viñas Winery and Oil Mill. A space that awakens the interest of art lovers with different techniques from national and international artists.
